## Installation **Command** ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/toggle-group ``` Installing the group also installs `toggle`, because the items share its variant classes. **Manual** Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI. 1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed. ```package-manager npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react class-variance-authority ``` 2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers. - [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency. - [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency. - [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency. - [@cadence/toggle](https://cadence.dev/r/toggle.json) — direct registry dependency. 3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines. | Item | Target file | Full source | | --- | --- | --- | | cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) | | cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) | | cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/provider.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/popup-style.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | toggle | `@components/cadence/toggle/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/toggle.json) | | toggle-group | `@components/cadence/toggle-group/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/toggle-group.json) | [Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) [Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) [Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) [Source files: toggle](https://cadence.dev/r/toggle.json) [Source files: toggle-group](https://cadence.dev/r/toggle-group.json) 4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition. No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme. The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once: ```tsx import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider"; export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { return {children}; } ``` Copy all ten target files, preserving the sibling `toggle/`, `toggle-group/` and shared `lib/` directories, relative imports and `"use client"` directives. The group imports Toggle's variant classes, and its default item renderer reaches `press-button.tsx`, `control-animation.tsx` and `native-div.tsx`. Copy every file in the listed payloads; the provider files and `motion` package are required imports even without an application provider wrapper. Complete the base theme setup linked above and ensure Tailwind scans the copied files. No additional item-specific CSS or external asset is required. In full, `feedback.press` scales item content, `layout.shared` moves a decorative fill within each single-selection group, and `state.morph` fades/scales local fills in multiple selection. Reduced drops press scale and shared travel but keeps local opacity feedback; none settles all three immediately. Standalone groups follow the system motion preference. The optional `CadenceProvider` controls mode and timing; a nested full scope still respects system reduced motion. Usage, the top specimen, Multiple and Vertical use icons. They need this example-only package; Toggle Group itself does not: ```package-manager npm install lucide-react ``` Controlled also needs [Button](/components/button): ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button ``` For manual installation, follow Button's Manual tab and add `button/index.tsx`. Its npm dependencies and shared files are already in this installation graph. The other examples need only Toggle Group and its included helpers. The site's preview shell is not consumer setup. In Next.js App Router, Segmented with a required selection and Controlled need client modules for `useState`, change handlers and the external button's click handler. Usage, Visual variants, Multiple, Spacing, Vertical, Sizes, Disabled and Explicit motion scopes can be composed in synchronous Server Components with the shown JSX and serializable props. Caller refs, event handlers, function-valued `render`, `className(state)` or `style(state)`, and client hooks such as `useState` or `useRef` need a caller client boundary. Keep the installed sources' client directives. Give each item a stable, nonempty `value`. The group owns pressed state through an array: use `defaultValue` for uncontrolled initial values, or `value` with `onValueChange` for controlled values. Single selection is the default and allows an empty array when the selected item is pressed again; `multiple` allows independent values. To require one selection, use the shown caller policy that ignores empty requests. Group values take precedence over item `pressed` / `defaultPressed`; `details.cancel()` in an item or group change handler can veto a change. The group renders `role="group"`, and items are native `type="button"` buttons with `aria-pressed`. Name the group and every icon-only item. Tab enters the enabled controls; horizontal arrows or vertical Up/Down move focus without selecting, Home/End reach the ends, and Space/Enter toggle the focused item. `loopFocus` defaults to true; false stops at either end. Disabled items are skipped and cannot activate; disabling the group retains its values. For RTL arrow navigation, use Base UI's `DirectionProvider` from `@base-ui/react/direction-provider` with `direction="rtl"`, as well as RTL document direction. Group size and variant are inherited by items; `spacing` sets the gap, and zero joins adjacent pressed fills in multiple selection. Nested groups have separate value, appearance and shared-fill scopes. These buttons do not generate hidden inputs or submit the selected array through `name` or item `value`, and do not expose a submit-button `type` or `form` association. If a form needs these values, map caller-owned state to explicit form fields and handle reset in the caller. The caller owns business data, persistence, required-selection rules, validation, error text and any `aria-invalid` / `aria-describedby` association. Native animation and drag handlers, state-based classes/styles and refs pass through the default renderer. A caller item `render` replaces its press renderer while retaining the supplied decorative fill and content children; spread the supplied props, including children, and preserve the ref and button semantics. Keep `nativeButton` consistent with the rendered element. ## Usage ```tsx import { AlignCenter, AlignLeft, AlignRight } from "lucide-react"; import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/toggle-group"; export function Alignment() { return ( ); } ``` ## Visual variants Default, outline and segmented are fixed, independent single-selection groups. Each starts on Week; clicking its selected item clears it. ```tsx import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/toggle-group"; export function GroupVariants() { return (
{(["default", "outline", "segmented"] as const).map((variant) => ( Day Week Month ))}
); } ``` ## Multiple Multiple permits independent marks. Adjacent pressed fills join at zero spacing. Pressing Bold off does not change Italic. ```tsx import { BoldIcon, ItalicIcon, UnderlineIcon } from "lucide-react"; import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/toggle-group"; export function MultipleGroup() { return ( ); } ``` ## Segmented with a required selection The caller ignores empty arrays to require one selection. The pill style alone does not require a value or select a newly focused item. ```tsx "use client"; import { useState } from "react"; import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/toggle-group"; export function SegmentedGroup() { const [range, setRange] = useState(["week"]); return ( { if (next.length) setRange(next); }} aria-label="Time range" > Day Week Month ); } ``` ## Spacing Zero spacing joins adjacent pressed fills; one spacing step separates them. Both groups retain independent multiple selection and an outer strip. ```tsx import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/toggle-group"; export function GroupSpacing() { return (
{[0, 1].map((spacing) => ( Bold Italic Underline ))}
); } ``` ## Vertical A fixed vertical group lays out items in a column and uses Up/Down for roving focus. Focus alone does not change selection. ```tsx import { AlignCenterIcon, AlignLeftIcon, AlignRightIcon } from "lucide-react"; import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/toggle-group"; export function VerticalGroup() { return ( ); } ``` ## Sizes Small, default and large items are 32, 36 and 40px tall. These three horizontal groups use their own fixed size, inherited by each item. ```tsx import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/toggle-group"; export function GroupSizes() { return (
{(["sm", "default", "lg"] as const).map((size) => ( Day Week ))}
); } ``` ## Controlled The value is always an array, including for a single-selection group. The external alignment button changes only this caller-owned value; choosing the selected item can clear it. ```tsx "use client"; import { useState } from "react"; import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/toggle-group"; export function ControlledGroup() { const [value, setValue] = useState(["center"]); return (

); } ``` ## Disabled The first group skips a disabled middle item when moving focus and uses loopFocus={false} to stop at either end. The default is to wrap focus. The second disables the whole group and retains its selected Day. ```tsx import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/toggle-group"; export function DisabledGroups() { return (
Day Week Month Day Week
); } ``` ## Explicit motion scopes The first group is fixed to none from its first DOM appearance. A second provider explicitly selects full inside that outer none scope; the system reduced-motion preference still wins. First Second

Identifies the item. | | `disabled` | `boolean`| `false` | Keeps it visible but unpressable. | | `className` | `string` / state callback | – | Merged last. | The default press button preserves native React `onAnimationStart`, `onDrag`, `onDragStart` and `onDragEnd` events, including capture and cancellation. Callback and object refs follow the same button; replacing a callback runs its React 19 cleanup before assigning the next ref. A caller `render` replaces the default renderer and owns spreading its supplied props. ## Motion contract Single selection uses one shared decorative fill scoped to each group. Multiple selection keeps one local fill per item. Neither changes the buttons' layout boxes; corner changes that join neighboring fills are immediate state styling. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ---------------- | ---------------- | ------------- | | press | `scale 1 → 0.97` | `feedback.press` | yes | | release | `scale 0.97 → 1` | `feedback.press` | yes | | single selection | fill transform between items | `layout.shared` | yes | | multiple selection | fill opacity and `scale 0.96 → 1` | `state.morph` | yes | | reduced | shared fill jumps; local fills fade; no press scale | – | – | | none | immediate selection, opacity and press state; zero duration | – | – | Press scale applies only to the content, keeping the button and decorative fill in the group's common stacking context. A travelling fill stays below all labels and icons, including the items it crosses and the focused destination. Full mode uses the velocity-preserving shared spring. Reduced, none and a zero recipe clock render a static single-selection fill, cancelling an in-flight projection without replacing the focused button. Local fills keep opacity under reduced and settle immediately under none. All animated parts expose `data-motion`; every duration, scale and spring comes from Cadence tokens. ## Keyboard interactions | Keys | Action | | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------- | | `Tab` | Enters the group at the last pressed item. | | `Arrow Right/Down` | Moves focus to the next item. | | `Arrow Left/Up` | Moves focus to the previous item. | | `Space` / `Enter` | Presses the focused item. | With `loopFocus` (default) the arrows wrap around at the ends. ## Accessibility - The group renders `role="group"`; each item is a `
